summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of Addison’s disease, hypothyroidism, and hypertension, was admitted for abdominal discomfort, nausea, vomiting, and bilateral lower extremity weakness, consistent with an adrenal crisis. She had doubled her prednisone prior to admission with partial relief. Labs showed hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and acute kidney injury likely due to prerenal causes from poor oral intake. She received IV hydrocortisone and fluids in the emergency department and improved rapidly. Her electrolytes normalized, symptoms resolved, and she tolerated a regular diet. A right lower extremity ultrasound ruled out DVT; leg pain was attributed to overuse and old tendon injury. She was discharged on a 2-day hydrocortisone taper, resumed her baseline prednisone and Florinef, restarted metoprolol, and had Celexa increased to 20mg daily. Follow-up was advised with her primary care provider.
